article.story: NEW YORK -- — Jalen Brunson scored 30 points, Mikel Bridges hit the winning 3-pointer at the buzzer, and the New York Knicks edged the Portland Trail Blazers 97-96 on Saturday night. The defending champions led by 26 points in the first half before Portland charged back and took a 96-94 lead with 3.4 seconds left after a pair of free throws from Deni Avdija. New York called a timeout to advance the ball past half court and Josh Hart found Bridges on the wing as Toumani Camara leapt past him. Bridges calmly hit his second 3-pointer of the night before he was mobbed by his teammates. Brunson scored 19 of his 30 points in the first quarter and Landry Shamet had 20 for the Knicks, who won their fourth consecutive game on a night they honored 50 alumni. Donovan Clingan finished with 22 points and 13 rebounds, and Avdija had 20 for Portland, who have lost three of their last four games — all on the road. The Knicks led 66-43 at the break — the fewest points they have allowed in the first half this season — before Portland mounted its rally. The Trail Blazers — whose 43 points over the first two quarters were a season low — outscored New York 29-15 in the third period and cut the deficit to six points with 58 seconds remaining in the quarter before Shamet’s 3-pointer extended the Knicks lead to 81-72. Portland fell behind by 13 after a 3-point play from Tyler Kolek extended the New York lead 92-79. Camara and Lillard scored consecutive baskets before Jose Alvarado’s layup made it 94-84. Lillard then sparked a 12-0 run capped by Advija’s free throws after he was fouled by Andre Drummond, who attempted to strip the ball away, before Bridges’ last-second 3. Up Next Trail Blazers: Visit Philadelphia on Monday night. Knicks: Host Indiana on Sunday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
